I would not recommend this clinic based on my experience. I brought my 11-year-old cat in because he has recurring vomiting and episodes of bright-red blood in his stool. I felt that the veterinarian did not spend enough time evaluating him or listening carefully to his symptoms and history.

I was told that my cat had FIP based on his bloodwork and X-rays. Because this was extremely concerning, I sought multiple additional veterinary opinions. The other veterinarians I consulted disagreed with the interpretation and did not believe the findings supported an FIP diagnosis, particularly given that my cat does not display the typical symptoms associated with FIP.

What was especially frustrating was how quickly the diagnosis was made without, in my opinion, a thorough evaluation or discussion of other possible causes for his symptoms. The visit was also extremely expensive, which was difficult to accept when I felt my concerns weren’t being adequately heard or addressed.

When it comes to your pet, you want to trust that you’re receiving careful, thorough, and compassionate care. Unfortunately, I left this clinic feeling more worried and confused than when I arrived. After getting multiple opinions elsewhere, I am very glad I did not rely on the initial diagnosis alone.

Based on my experience, I would not return to this clinic.

My mom and I brought my dog in today (July 4, 2026) while they were open. We were actually reccommended by the VCA Animal Specialists of the Valley on Ventura. We needed an Urgent Care and this was the first that was open today because of the holiday.

We roll in at 5:55 after being told the vet would be seeing walk-in patients at 6pm. It turned out, HE WASN'T EVEN THERE! The front desk girl, Cheyenne, said he'd be a few minutes because (and she told us this while laughing) "someone walked into his house and stole his pizza off the counter." She acted like it was some big joke and then said "He's the only vet I know who has had his house broken into so many times."

FIrst of all, unprofessional as HELL! Second, why are you laughing about your boss's house getting broken into? Third, why are you even telling us this??????

Now, it wasn't a life or death emergency, but it's called Urgent Care for a reason. We had to do the new patient paperwork on the iPad and then she had to ask us questions so we sat there for maybe 10 minutes. We saw a man walk in, but didn't know if it was the vet or not. It was the doctor, Dr. Gurmani. He never introduced himself either, I only know his name because I just looked up who owned the clinic. He does.

She brings us into a room becasue she has to take my dog's temperature and tells us she's "sorry that this one takes so long to count. I took the fast one home." Also while laughing. WHYYYYYYYY are you taking office medical supplies home? Why are you telling us?

FINALLY the doctor comes in. He clearly has some sort of speech impediment so he speaks very softly and briefly. No problem, that doesn't bother us at all. We were told "he has a hard time speaking" though. But he doesn't explain anything let alone even look at my dog closely. He shined some sort of little light device in her eye, from a good distance, and said they would flush it and do a thing with drops to see if there was damage.

We thought she had been scratched by my grandma's cat.

Then the tech comes to get the dog and she immediately freaks out upon seeing him. This guy did not give off good vibes and when he noticed that she was clearly upset, he did......NOTHING. He just had my mom walk with them to the backroom door where he then pretty much had to drag her with him because she was so scared of him.

The front desk girl has us come back to the front after a few minutes and pay. No explanations, no doctor telling us what's up, NOTHING. So we go pay. She does breakdown the costs and gives a brief explanation of what each thing was after we asked. She then literally LAUGHS at my mom, inturrupts to correct her, and is snarky about the way we are paying. "I've never seen it done that way" and "That's actually so much easier than what you were doing." Like girl, that's NOT how you talk to a customer. We just had no words for the unprofessionalism.

A few minutes into this, the tech comes out with my dog who is practically dragging him to me because she wants to get away from him. Now, this tech is NOT listed on the website so I don't know his name. But Cheyenne claimed he was "a vet too" when he answered a question. This guy was OBVIOUSLY a vet tech. He gave me the medication and told me how to do it. He didn't talk to us otherwise.

I know this is really long, but I sincerely hope you (the vet, receptionist, other people looking for a vet) take the time to read it through. I've worked retail and am currently a teacher and I have NEVER even THOUGHT ABOUT talking to anyone in my work environment the way Cheyenne talked to us.

TLDR:

Pros: The place was clean. There was no wait, which probably was a bad sign.
Cons: Unprofessional staff. Uncommunicative vet. Overpriced.

Next time, in a non-life threatening case, I will wait the weekend and see my vet whom I adore and TRUST.

Thanks for reading.

My experience was heartbreaking. Throughout my cat's treatment, I never felt that I received a clear explanation of what was actually wrong with her. At the same time, cremation services were being discussed. It felt overwhelming and deeply lacking in compassion during one of the most painful moments of my life.

He likely went hours without relief, and his health deteriorated quickly.

They called again late that night, but I missed the call because I was asleep with my daughter. When I followed up, they told me everything was fine and that he was improving. We called once more since no updates were being provided and were told again that he was eating, drinking, urinating, and not ready to be picked up yet. That was completely false.

Eventually, I got a call from a staff member named Stephanie. I was hopeful it was to pick up Seven, but instead I received a cold voicemail saying he wasn’t doing well and that I needed to call back. When I did, she bluntly told me the vet was recommending euthanasia. I was in complete shock. I asked for time to process and speak with my husband, but instead I was bombarded with calls and felt incredibly pressured to put him down.

After I broke down emotionally on the phone, the vet suddenly changed his stance and said he’d try treatment for a few more days and even proceed with surgery. This sudden flip felt manipulative and confusing.

They did refund us what we paid and then some, but that doesn’t undo the emotional trauma or justify how dishonest and careless they were with our cat’s life. We were misled at every step and denied the chance to make informed decisions.
